versions.summary: Pre-versioned Plate Next package review. This is historical enrollment, not a current-pattern attestation.
migrationChecks: Run a full package review against the latest Plate Next doctrine.

versions.summary: Versioned Plate Next baseline with package-level proof and source-fingerprint drift detection.
migrationChecks: For a v0 package, rerun the full current package-review checklist.
Record focused proof, autoreview closure, the final package source fingerprint, current registry status, and then plan-checker closure.

versions.summary: Unified plugin authoring through repeated .extend() contributions with .withComponent() as the sole ordinary node binding.
migrationChecks: Migrate every specialized plugin builder declaration and usage in the package to repeated .extend() contributions.
Prove applicable api, read, selectors, update, extension, and codecs inference, including dependencies between ordered stages.
Replace ordinary direct render.node binding with .withComponent() before the terminal consumer .configure() call.
Audit the package for compatibility aliases, shims, deprecations, forwarding wrappers, and stale documentation for the rejected builder methods.

versions.summary: One .extend() call per plugin by default; repeat only for a genuine typed capability dependency.
migrationChecks: Merge independent plugin author contributions into one .extend() object or callback.
Keep multiple ordered .extend() stages only when a later contribution genuinely consumes a type introduced by an earlier stage.
Prove every surviving multi-stage chain through source inspection and focused type or runtime coverage.

versions.summary: Plate Next plan templates use the unified .extend({ extension }) contribution and reject stale specialized-builder wording.
migrationChecks: Audit plugin-owned editor extension contributions for .extend({ extension }) authoring.
Reject extendExtension declarations, calls, compatibility aliases, and plan evidence.
Audit plugin export inference wording and source for specialized .extend* builder assumptions.

versions.summary: One plugin-owned HTML codec contribution may carry a non-empty ordered rule tuple without another .extend() stage.
migrationChecks: Keep one schema-aware text/html rule or one non-empty ordered rule tuple under the plugin's codecs contribution.
Merge multiple HTML representations owned by one plugin into that single contribution.
Reject repeated .extend() stages justified only by representation count rather than an actual earlier-stage type dependency.

versions.summary: Plugin codec authoring uses the context-bound defineCodecs helper as the sole inference anchor.
migrationChecks: Author codec maps only through .extend(({ defineCodecs }) => ({ codecs: defineCodecs(...) })).
Use defineCodecs(map) for self and product maps and defineCodecs(TargetPlugin, map) for foreign maps.
Reject direct codecs objects, specialized codec builders, manual target fields, casts, and callback annotations.

versions.summary: Extracted reusable Plate editor-extension factories use the callback context's defineEditorExtension inference anchor.
migrationChecks: Keep inline extension objects plain because .extend() already contextually types them.
Make extracted reusable Plate extension factories return context.defineEditorExtension(...) so nested command, input, state, transaction, and dependency types remain inferred.
Keep the factory in the plugin's default single .extend() contribution and distinguish the context helper from the standalone defineEditorExtension imported from @platejs/plite.

versions.summary: Plugin constructors own every independent declaration field; root-level component replaces withComponent.
migrationChecks: Move independent api, read, selectors, update, extension, codecs, and static contributions into createBasePlugin or createPlatePlugin.
Keep .extend() only for builder context, imported or prebuilt declarations, or a real earlier-stage type dependency.
Declare component in createPlatePlugin or one terminal .configure({ component }); convert base descriptors through toPlatePlugin first.
Delete withComponent and reject public render.node authoring across source, docs, tests, and release guidance.
Prove constructor inference through source typecheck, declaration emit, dependency composition, conversion, and terminal configuration.

versions.summary: Base and static consumers bind components without importing the React plugin layer.
migrationChecks: Reject platejs/react, @platejs/core/react, and @platejs/*/react imports from Base kits, static renderers, and other Base/static modules.
Bind static components through terminal BasePlugin.configure({ component }) while keeping createBasePlugin renderer-neutral.
Bind Base/static descriptors to static renderer modules rather than live/client node components.
Keep toPlatePlugin(BasePlugin) only in live React adapter construction and delete conversion calls used solely by Base/static component binding.
Prove the Base terminal component type and runtime publication, static HTML rendering, zero forbidden imports, and live React kit preservation.

versions.summary: Plugin constructors own every independent contribution and its typed context callback.
migrationChecks: Move constructor-accessible api, read, selectors, update, extension, codecs, handlers, renderers, shortcuts, rules, and other static fields out of .extend().
Reject builder context alone as a reason for .extend(); constructor callbacks already receive the typed authoring context.
Keep .extend() only for imported or prebuilt descriptor adaptation, a shared factory inaccessible from the constructor, or a real earlier-stage type dependency.
Prove every surviving direct constructor .extend() chain through exact source enforcement, package typecheck, declaration emit, and focused runtime coverage.

versions.summary: Extracted editor-extension factories remain constructor-owned unless they require accumulated plugin context.
migrationChecks: Keep an extracted editor-extension factory in the plugin constructor when constructor context can invoke it.
Use one .extend() stage only when the factory needs accumulated plugin context, adapts an imported or prebuilt descriptor, or consumes an earlier capability.
Prove every surviving factory-owned .extend() stage through exact source enforcement, package typecheck, declaration emit, and focused runtime coverage.

versions.summary: React hook definitions live in one separate hook-family owner and never in plugin descriptors, component files, stores, or providers.
migrationChecks: Move every hook definition out of plugin descriptor, component, store, provider, and generic utility files into the matching use<Family>.ts[x] hook-family owner.
Merge related public and private subcomponent hooks into one hook-family file instead of creating one file per hook.
Keep plugin descriptors focused on plugin authoring and non-hook private implementation, with shared event or state primitives in an independent owner when needed to prevent import cycles.
Colocate hook tests beside the hook-family owner and prove exports, type inference, runtime behavior, and cycle-free import direction.

versions.summary: Plugin exports inline complete builder chains instead of routing through one-use private descriptor constants.
migrationChecks: Audit production plugin owners for private createBasePlugin, createPlatePlugin, or toPlatePlugin descriptors referenced only by one exported builder chain.
Inline one-use descriptor constants into the exported plugin chain while preserving every justified capability stage.
Keep a private descriptor only when it is installed or returned as a durable runtime identity, reused by multiple production owners, or required at a real external boundary.

versions.summary: Plugin runtime values use initialState and scoped per-editor stores without deleted option accessors or a parallel config channel.
migrationChecks: Replace plugin descriptor defaults and overrides with initialState and .configure({ initialState }).
Replace builder option accessors with inferred store and consumer access with editor.plugin(Plugin).store.get/set/subscribe.
Replace React option subscriptions with usePluginStore or useEditorPluginStore.
Reject deleted getOption, getOptions, setOption, setOptions, usePluginOption, top-level options, and parallel immutable config channels while preserving generic operation options.

versions.summary: Plugin capabilities have one semantic boundary protocol and one constructor-first authoring-stage protocol.
migrationChecks: Classify every contribution as initialState, store, selectors, api, read, update, extension, or codecs and reject any contribution with no honest owner.
Move pure store projections to selectors, supplied-state document queries to read, document mutations to update, and non-snapshot plugin services to api.
Reserve extension for genuine editor-wide Plite substrate; reject plugin-scoped state, reads, services, or updates republished through editor-wide extensions.

Move every independent contribution into createBasePlugin or createPlatePlugin; keep .extend() only for imported or prebuilt adaptation, a constructor-inaccessible shared factory, or a real earlier-capability type dependency.
Keep .configure() terminal and non-widening, preserve contextual inference, and prove every surviving .extend() by naming the capability type or external declaration it consumes.

versions.summary: Plugin callbacks use their current-owner context directly without confusing cross-plugin or editor-wide capabilities.
migrationChecks: Audit plugin authoring callbacks for editor.plugin(currentPlugin), current-key root api/read/update groups, editor.getPlugin(currentKey), and editor.getType(currentKey).
Replace same-owner lookups with supplied store, api, read, update, type, plugin, or installed values and remove unused editor or plugin destructuring.
Classify every surviving editor access as editor-wide substrate, cross-plugin access, one-shot transaction metadata, or a specialized callback contract that does not expose owner shortcuts.
Do not move, split, or wrap a coherent declaration solely to manufacture a shortcut; repair the owning Core contextual type when a documented shortcut is exposed but loses inference.
Prove the migration with affected package and app typechecks plus exact source scans across package, registry, and public plugin-authoring examples.

versions.summary: State-owning production descriptors publish an explicit state contract and check owner defaults without inference casts.
migrationChecks: Audit every state-owning production descriptor for a named *PluginState contract, exported whenever its descriptor is exported.
Check owner defaults through a typed constant or explicit factory return type; reject state contracts inferred from default objects, as casts, and satisfies patches.
Keep consumer .configure({ initialState }) overrides inline and partial instead of redeclaring the complete state contract.
Prove the state contract, default values, partial overrides, and exported descriptor inference with package typecheck and focused declaration or runtime coverage.

versions.summary: Plugin authoring explicitly rejects deleted builder helpers and routes same-key optional-kit membership to the composition owner.
migrationChecks: Audit plugin-builder chains, tests, examples, and docs for extendApi, extendEditorApi, extendSelectors, extendTx, extendTxGroup, extendExtension, extendCodecs, and extendHtmlCodec; classify the receiver so same-named non-plugin builders remain untouched.

Hard-delete every matching Plate plugin-builder helper, alias, shim, forwarding wrapper, export, and documentation path; author capabilities through the constructor or an honest staged .extend() contribution.
Audit same-key descriptors across independently optional app or registry kits as membership ownership, not mechanical deduplication; route unresolved public composition identity to best-api.
Prove the final package shape with focused source audits, package typecheck and behavior tests, plus optional-kit composition coverage when same-key descriptors exist.

versions.summary: Extension ownership uses the exact flat Plite descriptor vocabulary and rejects plugin-scoped behavior hidden in extension declarations.
migrationChecks: Audit extension declarations for the flat Plite descriptor vocabulary: activate, afterPublish, stateFields, effectTypes, facetProviders, selectionKinds, commands, corrections, contributions, config, tx, read, api, and on.*.
Reject stale extension field aliases, nested lifecycle bags, and plugin-scoped state, reads, services, or updates routed through extension.
Keep descriptor-owned read middleware and genuine root editor capabilities in extension; keep plugin-scoped read, api, selectors, and update on the plugin owner.
Prove the final extension shape with the schema-adoption checker, package typecheck, and focused lifecycle or capability behavior tests.

versions.summary: Extension authoring names raw descriptor declarations precisely and keeps plugin-scoped capabilities on the plugin owner.
migrationChecks: Treat constructor and justified staged extension values as built extensions or raw descriptor declarations, not legacy extension option bags.
Keep activation, state fields, effect types, commands, corrections, root capabilities, and descriptor-owned read middleware on extension.
Reject plugin-scoped state, reads, services, and updates hidden behind extension declarations.
Prove the final doctrine fingerprint, generated skill parity, schema-adoption checker, package typecheck, and focused behavior tests.

versions.summary: Registry cleanup preserves explicit teaching declarations and durable package semantic owners.
migrationChecks: Preserve explicit feature plugin, kit, renderer, and dependency declarations in registry examples when metadata names the feature kit or the example intentionally teaches its binding, even if EditorKit installs the descriptor transitively.
Reject package cleanup that copies a transform, query, navigation controller, or cross-layer algorithm into app or registry JSX; reuse the scoped capability or keep a flat standalone package owner.
Prove affected example install metadata, package exports and behavior, focused app typing, generated skill parity, and the relevant Browser demo routes.

versions.summary: Transparent registry feature wiring installs each descriptor exactly once.
migrationChecks: When an example explicitly teaches a feature descriptor already present in EditorKit, filter that descriptor from EditorKit by key and add or configure it explicitly once.
Reject both failure modes: deleting the explicit teaching declaration and installing duplicate same-key runtime descriptors.
Prove registry metadata alignment, focused app typing, generated skill parity, and the relevant Browser demo without duplicate-plugin diagnostics.

versions.summary: Plate extension fields own contextual typing without a duplicate context identity helper.
migrationChecks: Return plain extension objects from Plate constructors and .extend() callbacks, preserving nested command, input, state, transaction, dependency, and plugin-state inference.
Reject and delete Plate context identity helpers, aliases, annotations, casts, and any-based workarounds that compensate for a broken extension-field generic.
Keep Plate context capture inside authoring callbacks, extract domain inputs, and reserve Plite defineEditorExtension for independently reusable standalone descriptors.
